title: NOUNS AFTER HOURS
status: Original developed series concept; scripts ready for illustration and adaptation
tagline: They finished the tasks. Now they need a life.
logline: When ten visual bot companions clock out, they inherit the nightly care of a forgotten neighborhood cinema—and discover that a useful life needs a little useless magic.
premise: At midnight, the companion window on a desktop becomes a door to Offscreen, a neighborhood of things nobody has clicked in years. The ten Nouns find The Between, a small cinema whose screen has gone blank. A brass instruction plate says OPEN FOR WHAT? Over ten nights, they try to run the place with the habits that made them useful at work. Each habit helps. Each habit also gets in the way. The cinema becomes worth reopening when they stop treating friendship as another task to complete.

world.neighborhood: Offscreen: one walkable block, a cinema, a record stall, a rooftop, a garden arcade and an alley that looks longer in the rain.
world.home: The Between: forty mismatched chairs, a temperamental projector, a tiny box office, an unfinished marquee, a cabinet of paper ephemera and a roof that catches the dawn.
world.timeRule: Each issue occupies one midnight-to-dawn visit. The companions return to their daytime windows at dawn. Night ten is the opening; future nights allow the series to continue.
world.scaleRule: Original pixel portraits remain untouched. Expression comes from the surrounding pose frame, props, typography, camera and timing. Character scale is deliberately theatrical rather than anatomically literal.
world.technologyRule: No all-powerful assistant, sentient-money system or magical internet search resolves a story. Characters solve problems through observation, making, conversation and asking for help.
world.residentRule: The initial ten-issue run shows only the ten established companions as speaking characters. Other neighborhood life is suggested through empty coats, handwritten notes, shoes by a door and distant silhouettes without borrowed likenesses.
world.cinemaRule: The screen can show a programmed film, shadows or a blank field. It cannot read minds. Scenes that resemble a genre are the characters playing, rehearsing or interpreting their own situation.

tone.promise: Warm workplace comedy after the workplace closes; miniature adventure with real feeling and small, readable visual jokes.
tone.comedyEngine: A genuinely useful trait becomes a beautifully overbuilt response to an ordinary human problem. The correction is relational rather than humiliating.
tone.emotionalEngine: They are used to being valued for what they do. The cinema gives them somewhere to be valued for who they are.
tone.ratingDirection: Broad teen-and-adult appeal; no graphic violence, sexual material or cruel humiliation in this first season.
tone.dialogue: Compact, dry and generous. Characters disagree without becoming mean. No copied catchphrases, celebrity voices or imitation endorsements.
visualGrammar: Original Nouns geometry with a two-ink night palette and one warm accent.
Wide still frames interrupted by a precise prop gag.
Inventive empty space: an unfilled form can become a stage, a blank note a dedication.
A physical paper object concludes every issue, but the feeling concludes the story.

seasonArc.question: What is The Between supposed to be open for?
progression: Nights 1–3: find the space, choose a way through it, recover its unfinished history.
Nights 4–6: learn how the place should feel, look and invite participation.
Nights 7–9: learn how to host, make room for absence and share responsibility.
Night 10: assemble the notes, reveal the complete sentence and open the doors.
seasonArc.reveal: The ten collected reverse fragments read: A PLACE TO BE MORE THAN WHAT YOU DO NEXT. It is a sentence they have earned, not a prophecy that made the choices for them.
seasonArc.ending: The first program is an imperfect live shadow show. Ten mismatched chairs face the screen. The last shot leaves one extra chair for whoever arrives next.
seasonArc.seasonTwoDoor: A neighboring rooftop radio station begins broadcasting room tone. Nobody knows whether it is a mistake or the best show in town.

botMoney.purpose: Dated printed souvenirs of a moment, not money accepted for goods or entry. Treasury makes one small edition after each night.
botMoney.denominations: Playful measures such as 1 BEGINNING, 4 BEATS or 10 BELONGINGS. Numerals describe the series; they do not promise financial value.
botMoney.visibleLabel: COLLECTIBLE ART • NO CASH VALUE • NO REDEMPTION
botMoney.useInStory: A note records an act of attention or care. Admission to the cinema is free. Nobody needs a note to belong.
botMoney.collectorHook: Ten portrait fronts; ten sentence fragments on the reverse; a full set can be arranged as a single paper mural. Collecting is optional and there is no rarity or resale promise.

creativeOdes.label: Creative ode 01 — Economical print wit
creativeOdes.periodLens: 1960s print-ad economy, interpreted as a design principle
creativeOdes.execution: One small object, one large truthful idea, one restrained headline. An empty chair under the line UNFILLED. NOT UNIMPORTANT.
creativeOdes.reason: Let the audience complete the joke. Use scale and white space instead of a paragraph explaining the brand.
creativeOdes.attributionBoundary: An original campaign direction; not work by, endorsed by or a recreation of a named historical agency.

creativeOdes.label: Creative ode 02 — The enormous small event
creativeOdes.periodLens: 1980s event-poster scale, interpreted as a design principle
creativeOdes.execution: A tiny paper ticket rendered like a celestial arrival; ten original Noun portraits at the horizon; the line TONIGHT, SOMETHING SMALL GETS BIG.
creativeOdes.reason: Give the act of showing up blockbuster importance while keeping the object intimate and handmade.
creativeOdes.attributionBoundary: An original campaign direction; no copied film composition, logo, credit block, recognizable character or studio endorsement.

welcome: Office sitcom rhythms without borrowed characters.
A heist whose treasure is the simplest route home.
Noir investigation of a missing credit.
A space-opera countdown that cannot improve a kettle.
An awards night for the least visible act of care.
Arcade competition redesigned so resting is allowed.
Record-store listening as friendship rather than expertise.
avoid: Copied dialogue, franchise costumes, signature logos or near-identical key art.
Pretending art-note collecting purchases membership or status.
Giving bots clinical, financial or spiritual authority.

formatSystem.comic: Ten four-page mini-issues. Page 1 cover; pages 2–3 six panels each; page 4 character extra, reader invitation and end card.
formatSystem.companion: Each issue connects to its real local companion tool: an optional creative activity, never a claim that the tool acts autonomously.
formatSystem.objects: A matching art note, postcard, shirt graphic and print-ad premise can carry a story outside the comic.
formatSystem.social: Short panel crops, prop-only jokes, silent loops, creator commentary and an optional community prompt. Publication is separate from preparing these assets.

authorshipAndArt.story: Original story, character personalities, dialogue and series design developed for this project.
authorshipAndArt.portraits: Original Nouns art from the existing project asset manifest; Nouns artwork is CC0. These new fictional personalities do not claim to represent minted token owners.
authorshipAndArt.provenanceInstruction: Preserve the exact existing companion portrait seeds, asset hash and license notices when illustrating. No AI redraw is required for identity.
